first.rationale: Competitive entry pricing creates an immediate acquisition risk in the price-sensitive SMB segment, where prior evidence indicates targeted promotional pricing can lift qualified acquisition and revenue. I will verify both the pricing result and the onboarding evidence before committing, because a targeted, time-bounded offer may protect demand but could reduce unit economics or attract lower-value customers. A small guarded test preserves learning while limiting discount-dependence risk.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. It directly addresses the 4% decline in completion and has verified evidence of higher completion (+13%), faster time-to-value (-2.1 days), and improved 30-day retention (+3%), supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is rejected because its verified acquisition lift came with a 12% 30-day retention decline, making it unsuitable for the primary objective despite competitive pressure.
